completion_data.completion_summary: Eliminated the per-entry echo|jq triple-spawn (literature-coverage-delta.sh) and the dominant echo|tr/echo|grep fork cost (literature-term-match.sh's to_lower/term_matches) with a single-pass jq @tsv extraction plus fork-free pure-bash term matching. Candidate-set equivalence proven clean across 7 queries against the live 292-doc corpus (full unbounded lists, byte-identical); a full-corpus non-ASCII/locale divergence audit found exactly 1 informational entry that did not manifest in any tested query. Wall time dropped from 132s to 1.7s (~76x) across the 7-query harness; test-lit-pipeline.sh --runtime passed 44/44 including all 6 Section H regression cases.

memory_candidates.content: In bash, `grep -oE 'candidates=[^ ]*'` (or any unanchored substring pattern) against a line that ALSO contains `delta_candidates=107` will spuriously match the embedded `candidates=107` substring inside that longer field name, corrupting downstream parsing. When parsing a fixed-shape space-delimited status line with similarly-named fields (e.g. `foo=X bar_foo=Y`), prefer positional word-splitting (`read -r f1 f2 ... <<< "$line"`) over field-name regex extraction — it sidesteps substring-of-fieldname collisions entirely, as long as you can bound how many space-free fields precede any field that may itself contain spaces.

For a bash equivalence-harness comparing two versions of a script that reads PROJECT_ROOT=SCRIPT_DIR/../.. and a file under $PROJECT_ROOT/specs/, you can create a fully isolated fake root per snapshot by nesting the script copy two directories deep (e.g. harness/before/fakeroot/scripts/script.sh) so PROJECT_ROOT resolves to harness/before/ and a fake specs/ subdirectory there never touches the real repo's specs/ tree. This avoids any risk of a benchmark/equivalence harness mutating real project state while still exercising the script's real path-resolution logic unmodified.
